newsitem.title: USA: Highlights of N.Y. State Gov's FY 1998 budget.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of N.Y. State Gov's FY 1998 budget.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki proposed Tuesday a $66.133 billion budget that raises spending by 2.2 percent but cuts the General Fund, which is funded by taxpayers, by $56 million to $32.83 billion.

Pataki, a Republican, noted that the General Fund spending marks a $782 million or 2.3 percent reduction from the 1994-1995 budget, the last one approved by the former administration, which was led by Mario Cuomo, a Democrat.

While Wall Street brokerage houses and banks, which are a vital economic engine for the state and for New York City, produced strong profits in 1996, the Pataki Administration said it is not counting on a third record year from this sector.
Highlights of the Pataki Administration's budget follow.
--Estimated surplus of $1.3 billion in fiscal 1997, following $445 million surplus in fiscal 1996.
--Proposed spending from all state funds, including those dedicated to specific program areas, estimated at $43.97 billion, up 1.2 percent.
--Adds $130 million to the state's Rainy Day Fund, bringing balance to an all-time high of $332 million.
--Calls for $65 million in Contingency Reserve Fund to protect against risks like litigation of federal disallowences.
--Estimated 1998 budget gap of $1.3 billion after $1.3 billion surplus in fiscal 1997.
